policies.title: Kosovo ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Kosovo national travelling on a Kosovo ordinary passport is classified as citizenship, rather than as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: Article 35 says Kosovo citizens may not be denied entry. This policy does not classify a dual national who presents another country's document.
It does not establish treatment for residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency or other special documents.

policies.title: Listed foreign ordinary passports: visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Kosovo's official embassy platform lists these nationalities as not requiring a short-stay visa, subject to later controlling amendments specified separately.
conditions: This is an ordinary-passport short-visitor classification. It does not turn the web contact form or a visa application form into an eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route.
The Interior Ministry states a maximum short stay of 90 days in each 180-day period; a valid travel document, purpose, means, address registration, and final admission requirements remain applicable.

The source also identifies biometric-ID-card arrangements for EU/Schengen, Holy See, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, Albania, Montenegro and Serbia. This policy records only their separately listed ordinary-passport baseline.

policies.title: Hong Kong and Macao travel documents: visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Kosovo expressly exempts valid travel documents issued by the administrations of Hong Kong and Macao from the visa requirement.
conditions: This is document-specific: it applies only to valid travel documents issued by the named Hong Kong or Macao administrations, not generally to Chinese, British, Portuguese or other documents.
It records entry treatment only and makes no recognition, citizenship, diplomatic, official, service, residence, work or transit inference.

policies.title: Taiwan travel documents: visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Kosovo exempts holders of Taiwan-issued travel documents; the 2024 controlling amendment removed the earlier advance-notification condition.
conditions: This is limited to a Taiwan-issued travel document and does not imply a Kosovo recognition, citizenship or diplomatic-status conclusion.
The embassy page's older two-week notification text is superseded by Decision No. 21/216, which expressly removes that notification requirement.
A visa waiver does not remove ordinary travel-document, purpose, means, registration or final-admission checks.

policies.title: Ukraine ordinary passport: temporary visa waiver
policies.summary: Government Decision No. 14/67 temporarily suspends Kosovo's entry-visa regime for Ukrainian citizens until a later Government decision.
conditions: The Gazette says the suspension remains effective until a subsequent Government decision; this candidate found no later official revocation, so recheck before publication.
No eVisa, ETA, arrival-visa, work, residence or special-document entitlement is established. Ordinary admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance visa required
policies.summary: For these foreign ordinary passports, Kosovo's official embassy guidance requires a Kosovo visa for a visit or transit; the listed application process is consular, not electronic issuance.
conditions: Applications are submitted in person to the relevant Kosovo diplomatic or consular mission. A web form is not evidence of electronic visa issuance, and no eVisa, ETA or nationality-wide visa-on-arrival route is established here.
The application guidance requires the supporting travel document, purpose, accommodation or means, health insurance and other specified evidence. A visa does not automatically confer entry.

For a visa-regime national, a valid biometric Schengen residence permit or valid multiple-entry Schengen visa may instead create a 15-day document-conditioned entry, transit and stay exemption; it does not change this ordinary-passport baseline.
Russia is expressly excluded from that Schengen-document exception by the 2022 Government decision; Russian ordinary, official and diplomatic passport holders remain required to obtain a Kosovo visa.

Botswana, Namibia and South Africa are visa-regime countries under Decision No. 21/216. This visa classification makes no entry-prohibition or recognition finding for any listed document, including PS.
Diplomatic/official exceptions, refugee/stateless travel documents, UN travel documents, work, residence and other special-document routes are not classified.

application.label: Kosovo consular short-stay visa procedure
application.processingTime: Apply in person no later than three months before the visit; the page does not give a decision-time promise.
steps: Apply in person to the relevant Kosovo diplomatic or consular mission.
Provide the completed original application, travel document, purpose and accommodation or means evidence, insurance and other requested documents.
Receive the visa decision before travel; the visa itself does not automatically confer entry.

conflicts.explanation: Decision No. 21/216 places Botswana under Kosovo's visa regime, superseding the older embassy list that still displays Botswana visa-free.
Decision No. 21/216 places Namibia under Kosovo's visa regime, superseding the older embassy list that still displays Namibia visa-free.

unresolved.reason: Signed Decision No. 14/280 adds Fiji to the visa regime but expressly enters into force on Official Gazette publication. The meeting report alone does not prove that publication, and no Gazette record was confirmed in this review.

Decision No. 02/237 expressly establishes Bosnia and Herzegovina entry only with a valid biometric identity card. No current Kosovo source reviewed directly establishes the ordinary-passport short-visitor treatment.
Singapore is absent from the official inbound visa-free country list and special categories reviewed. Omission is not treated as an advance-visa complement.

The reviewed guidance offers EU nationals a biometric-ID-card route but does not directly establish the ordinary-passport baseline for Slovenia, which is absent from the country list. No inference is made from the card route.
